Class AimMotor

java.lang.Object
dev.swordai.core.rl.AimMotor
public final class AimMotor extends Object
How a chosen camera speed becomes camera movement, modelled on a hand on a mouse.

The yaw and pitch heads pick the speed the agent wants. The hand takes that up gradually: each tick it closes only part of the gap between the speed it has and the speed that is wanted. A turn therefore builds up and dies away over a few ticks instead of jumping, and one odd choice moves the view only part of the way.

A hand at rest also stays at rest. It only gets going once the built-up push reaches BREAKAWAY, so a real turn starts at once while a single small impulse does nothing, and it comes to a dead stop as soon as the push has faded below REST_BELOW. Holding still is something the agent can do exactly, not a balance it has to keep.
